Hermès Stock Tumbles as Birkin Bag Maker Flags Slowdown
Shares of Hermes dropped as much as 12% Wednesday after the Birkin bag maker reported a slowdown in sales growth for the first quarter. If sustained, the fall would be the stock’s biggest drop since Hermes went public in 1993, according to FactSet data. Hermes flagged a weaker rate of growth in Asia compared with last year, as well as a hit from the conflict in the Middle East.

It offers systems integration and application management; security; intelligent platform; infrastructure; software engineering; data, AI, cloud; and automation and global delivery services. The company also operates business processes for specific enterprise functions, including finance and accounting, sourcing and procurement, supply chain, marketing and sales, and human resources, as well as industry-specific services, such as platform trust and safety, banking, insurance, network and health services; and designs, manufactures, and assembles automation equipment, robotics, and other commercial hardware products. It serves communications, media, and technology; financial services; banking and capital markets, and insurance; health and public service; consumer goods, retail, travel services; industrial; life science; and chemicals, natural resources, energy, and utilities sectors. Accenture plc has collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to deliver transformative digital services to public sector, defense, and national security organizations. It has a collaboration with OpenAI to help enterprise clients unlock new levels of innovation and growth by bringing agentic AI systems; has a strategic collaboration with Microsoft and Avanade for the development of an agentic factory intelligence system; and INFRONEER Holdings Inc. and SAP Japan Co., Ltd. to develop a new financial data and insights platform. It also has strategic partnership with Netomi, Inc. to help enterprises reinvent customer experience using agentic AI systems. The company has a strategic alliance with ServiceNow for integrated risk management and third-party risk management solutions. Accenture plc was founded in 1951 and is based in Dublin, Ireland.

businessOverview.why: International trade disputes as well as changes and uncertainty regarding international trade and trade policies, including the imposition or threat of the imposition of new or increased tariffs or other trade restrictions on goods from the countries where our manufacturers are located, could result in a materially adverse impact to our business.

evidence.quote: International trade disputes as well as changes and uncertainty regarding international trade and trade policies, including the imposition or threat of the imposition of new or increased tariffs or other trade restrictions on goods from the countries where our manufacturers are located, could result in a materially adverse impact to our business. During fiscal 2026, the primary manufacturers of Coach products were located in Vietnam, Cambodia, the Philippines and India, and the primary manufacturers of Kate Spade products were located in Vietnam, Cambodia, the Philippines, and Bangladesh. Increased tariffs or other trade restrictions against these countries, as well as any tariffs or other trade restrictions implemented by these countries in retaliation, could limit our ability to manufacture products in countries that have the labor and technical expertise needed. Further, we have developed strategies to mitigate the impact of additional tariffs; however, these strategies may not be effective, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

selected.text: Tapestry (TPR) Is Down 20.7% After Soft 2027 Outlook Tempers Dividend Hike And Buybacks
selected.context:
Tapestry (TPR) Is Down 20.7% After Soft 2027 Outlook Tempers Dividend Hike And Buybacks
Tapestry, Inc. has already reported fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 results, with sales rising to US$1,876.6 million and US$8,004.2 million respectively, alongside a swing from loss to profit and a Board-approved 16% increase in the quarterly dividend to US$0.4625 per share. The company also completed over US$1.11 billion of share repurchases under its 2025 program, even as guidance pointed to softer fiscal 2027 revenue expectations tied to ongoing weakness at Kate Spade despite strong momentum at Coach. Next, we'll assess how cautious fiscal 2027 sales guidance tied to Kate Spade's weakness reshapes Tapestry's longer-term investment narrative.

Slowing Growth And Margin Pressures Could Be A Game Changer For Tapestry (TPR)
Tapestry recently reported that weak constant currency growth over the past two years, higher expenses, and returns on capital under pressure are weighing on its underlying business performance. This combination of slowing momentum, operating margins below industry levels, and less effective investment outcomes raises fresh questions about the strength and efficiency of Tapestry’s operating model. We’ll now examine how Tapestry’s weaker constant currency growth and operational challenges may reshape the previously optimistic investment narrative for the company.

Why Tapestry (TPR) Is Up 12.5% After Raising Guidance On Coach Strength And Buybacks
In early February 2026, Tapestry, Inc. reported second‑quarter fiscal 2026 results showing higher sales of US$2,502.4 million and net income of US$561.3 million, while affirming a quarterly dividend of US$0.40 per share and completing a US$661.6 million share repurchase program. Beyond the headline beats, the company highlighted margin expansion, stronger performance at its Coach brand, and raised full‑year revenue and earnings guidance, underpinned by the acquisition of more than 3.7 million new customers and plans for US$1.5 billion in shareholder returns this fiscal year. We’ll now examine how Tapestry’s raised full‑year guidance and stronger Coach brand performance shape the company’s investment narrative.
